template.frontend-base.title: AI-RULES Frontend Base Template
template.frontend-base.desc.1: This is a frontend baseline rule set for React/Vue/Svelte style projects.
template.frontend-base.desc.2: Framework templates can extend this base and add framework-specific rules.
template.frontend-base.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.react-ts.title: AI-RULES React + TypeScript Template
template.react-ts.desc.1: This template extends the frontend base with React-specific rules.
template.react-ts.desc.2: Rules use the RULE block syntax for deterministic parsing and audit prompt generation.
template.react-ts.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be strengthened with ast-grep/semantic checks.
template.react-js.title: AI-RULES React + JavaScript Template
template.react-js.desc.1: This template extends the frontend base with React-specific rules for JavaScript projects.
template.react-js.desc.2: It keeps the same React architecture guidance without enabling TypeScript-only checks by default.
template.react-js.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be strengthened with ast-grep/semantic checks.
template.vue.title: AI-RULES Vue Template
template.vue.desc.1: This template extends frontend-base with Vue-specific rules for JavaScript or TypeScript projects.
template.vue.desc.2: It covers computed purity, list key stability, and DOM access constraints.
template.vue.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.electron.title: AI-RULES Electron Template
template.electron.desc.1: This template extends frontend-base for Electron renderer, preload, and main-process boundaries.
template.electron.desc.2: It focuses on renderer isolation, preload bridge safety, and desktop-specific security constraints.
template.electron.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.vscode-extension.title: AI-RULES VS Code Extension Template
template.vscode-extension.desc.1: This template extends frontend-base for VS Code extensions with webview and extension-host boundaries.
template.vscode-extension.desc.2: It focuses on command delegation, webview safety, and trusted workspace input handling.
template.vscode-extension.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.nodejs-base.title: AI-RULES Node.js Base Template
template.nodejs-base.desc.1: This template targets general Node.js services and transport/service/repository boundaries.
template.nodejs-base.desc.2: It covers transport layering, sensitive logging, timeout discipline, and centralized error handling.
template.nodejs-base.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.nodejs-express.title: AI-RULES Node.js + Express Template
template.nodejs-express.desc.1: This template extends nodejs-base with Express-specific transport and middleware rules.
template.nodejs-express.desc.2: It focuses on thin route handlers, explicit control flow, and error middleware discipline.
template.nodejs-express.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
template.nodejs-nestjs.title: AI-RULES Node.js + NestJS Template
template.nodejs-nestjs.desc.1: This template extends nodejs-base with NestJS controller and provider boundaries.
template.nodejs-nestjs.desc.2: It focuses on keeping controllers thin and stopping direct data-layer injection.
template.nodejs-nestjs.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
rule.ARCH-101.intent: UI components must not initiate network requests directly.
rule.ARCH-101.fix: Move request logic into the service layer and call services from UI components.
rule.ARCH-101.prompt.violation: Detected direct network request calls in UI layer.
rule.ARCH-101.prompt.requirement: UI components must not contain request logic.
rule.ARCH-101.prompt.solution: Move requests to services and reuse the existing API client.
rule.ARCH-102.intent: UI components must not access storage layer or databases directly.
rule.ARCH-102.fix: Move data access to server/service layer and expose through API boundaries.
rule.ARCH-102.prompt.violation: Detected data-layer or database access in UI layer.
rule.ARCH-102.prompt.requirement: UI layer must not depend on DB or ORM.
rule.ARCH-102.prompt.solution: Refactor access through service and API boundaries.
rule.ARCH-103.intent: Disallow reverse cross-layer dependencies (ui -> service -> data).
rule.ARCH-103.fix: Expose capabilities to UI via service abstractions.
rule.ARCH-103.prompt.requirement: Dependency direction must follow layering architecture.
rule.ARCH-103.prompt.solution: Refactor module boundaries and expose only service contracts.
rule.UI-201.intent: Prefer project UI library components over native HTML controls.
rule.UI-201.fix: Replace native tags with project UI components.
rule.UI-201.prompt.requirement: Use unified project UI components whenever possible.
rule.UI-201.prompt.solution: Replace with design-system components for consistency.
rule.UI-202.intent: Form controls must include accessibility labels.
rule.UI-202.fix: Add aria labels or bind labels properly.
rule.UI-202.prompt.violation: Detected form controls missing accessibility semantics.
rule.UI-202.prompt.solution: Add aria-label/aria-labelledby or explicit label linkage.
rule.FE-SEC-101.intent: Do not inject untrusted content through innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
rule.FE-SEC-101.fix: Remove raw HTML injection or sanitize content through a trusted sanitization layer before rendering.
rule.FE-SEC-101.prompt.violation: Detected raw HTML injection API usage in frontend code.
rule.FE-SEC-101.prompt.requirement: User-controlled content must not be rendered as raw HTML without strict sanitization.
rule.FE-SEC-101.prompt.solution: Replace raw HTML injection with safe rendering or a centralized sanitization utility.
rule.FE-SEC-102.intent: Do not dynamically execute frontend code through eval or Function constructors.
rule.FE-SEC-102.fix: Replace dynamic code execution with explicit logic, lookup tables, or validated parsers.
rule.FE-SEC-102.prompt.violation: Detected dynamic code execution in frontend code.
rule.FE-SEC-102.prompt.requirement: Frontend code must not execute arbitrary strings as code.
rule.FE-SEC-102.prompt.solution: Refactor dynamic execution into explicit safe control flow.
rule.FE-SEC-103.intent: Do not hardcode secrets, tokens, passwords, or API keys in frontend source code.
rule.FE-SEC-103.fix: Move sensitive values to secure backend-managed configuration or environment injection mechanisms.
rule.FE-SEC-103.prompt.violation: Detected likely hardcoded secret material in frontend code.
rule.FE-SEC-103.prompt.requirement: Sensitive credentials must not live in frontend source files.
rule.FE-SEC-103.prompt.solution: Remove the hardcoded value and replace it with secure configuration flow.
rule.FE-SEC-104.intent: User-controlled HTML, markdown, or dynamic URL content must not reach DOM rendering sinks without trusted sanitization or encoding.
rule.FE-SEC-104.fix: Route untrusted content through a centralized sanitization or safe-rendering layer before it reaches DOM sinks.
rule.FE-SEC-104.prompt.violation: Detected a likely XSS risk where untrusted content may flow into DOM rendering without trusted sanitization.
rule.FE-SEC-104.prompt.requirement: Untrusted rich content and dynamic URLs must be sanitized, encoded, or rendered through approved safe abstractions.
rule.FE-SEC-104.prompt.solution: Introduce a trusted sanitization boundary or replace the sink with safer rendering primitives.
rule.FE-SEC-105.intent: Externally hosted scripts in HTML entry points should use Subresource Integrity (SRI) when feasible.
rule.FE-SEC-105.fix: Add integrity and crossorigin attributes for third-party scripts, or self-host/version-pin the asset through trusted build tooling.
rule.FE-SEC-105.prompt.violation: Detected a third-party script tag without integrity protection.
rule.FE-SEC-105.prompt.requirement: Remote script includes should use Subresource Integrity or an equivalent trusted asset delivery strategy.
rule.FE-SEC-105.prompt.solution: Add SRI metadata and cross-origin settings, or move the dependency into a trusted local build pipeline.
rule.TS-401.fix: Replace any with explicit and safe types.
rule.TS-401.prompt.solution: Add concrete types for variables, params, and returns.
rule.STYLE-501.intent: Component names must be PascalCase and aligned with file names.
rule.STYLE-501.fix: Rename component to PascalCase and align file name.
rule.STYLE-501.prompt.requirement: Component and file naming should follow conventions.
rule.STYLE-501.prompt.solution: Normalize naming to PascalCase and update file names.
rule.STYLE-502.intent: Avoid large inline functions inside components.
rule.STYLE-502.fix: Extract logic into standalone functions or custom hooks.
rule.STYLE-502.prompt.violation: Detected oversized inline function in component.
rule.STYLE-502.prompt.requirement: Components should remain focused and maintainable.
rule.STYLE-502.prompt.solution: Move complex logic to hooks or utility modules.
rule.REACT-301.intent: Do not run side effects during render.
rule.REACT-301.fix: Move side effects to useEffect or event handlers.
rule.REACT-301.prompt.violation: Detected side effects during render phase.
rule.REACT-301.prompt.solution: Relocate side effects to lifecycle-safe locations.
rule.REACT-302.intent: Hooks can only be called in components or custom hooks.
rule.REACT-302.fix: Move hook invocations into component top-level or custom hooks.
rule.REACT-302.prompt.requirement: Hook call rules must be respected.
rule.REACT-302.prompt.solution: Refactor hook usage to legal call sites.
rule.REACT-303.intent: List rendering should not use unstable array index keys.
rule.REACT-303.fix: Use a stable domain identifier as the key instead of the loop index.
rule.REACT-303.prompt.violation: Detected list rendering keyed by array index.
rule.REACT-303.prompt.requirement: Rendered lists must use stable keys.
rule.REACT-303.prompt.solution: Replace index-based keys with stable entity identifiers.
rule.REACT-304.intent: Effects that fetch remote data must use stable dependency control.
rule.REACT-304.fix: Move request logic into a dedicated hook/service and make effect dependencies explicit and stable.
rule.REACT-304.prompt.violation: Detected effect-driven remote request with unstable or missing dependency discipline.
rule.REACT-304.prompt.requirement: Effects must not trigger stale, repeated, or looping requests.
rule.REACT-304.prompt.solution: Stabilize effect dependencies and isolate request logic into hooks/services.
rule.VUE-301.intent: Computed functions must remain pure and free of side effects.
rule.VUE-301.fix: Move side effects into watch or onMounted.
rule.VUE-302.intent: v-for must provide a stable key.
rule.VUE-302.prompt.requirement: List rendering must include stable keys.
rule.VUE-302.prompt.solution: Provide a unique key for each item.
rule.VUE-303.intent: Avoid direct DOM manipulation inside components.
rule.VUE-303.fix: Use refs or Vue-provided APIs for DOM access.
rule.VUE-303.prompt.requirement: DOM operations should be mediated by Vue.
rule.VUE-303.prompt.solution: Replace direct DOM access with ref/Vue APIs.
rule.VUE-304.intent: Props must not be mutated directly inside components.
rule.VUE-304.fix: Derive local state or emit updates instead of mutating props directly.
rule.VUE-304.prompt.violation: Detected direct prop mutation in a Vue component.
rule.VUE-304.prompt.requirement: Props are read-only inputs and must remain immutable inside components.
rule.VUE-304.prompt.solution: Create local state or emit update events instead of mutating props.
rule.VUE-305.intent: List rendering should not use the loop index as the key.
rule.VUE-305.fix: Use a stable unique identifier for :key instead of the loop index.
rule.VUE-305.prompt.violation: Detected :key bound to a loop index.
rule.VUE-305.prompt.requirement: Vue list keys must be stable across reorders and updates.
rule.VUE-305.prompt.solution: Replace index-based keys with a stable entity identifier.
rule.ELEC-301.intent: Renderer code must not import privileged Node.js built-ins directly.
rule.ELEC-301.fix: Move privileged access into preload or main-process services and expose only a narrow bridge to renderer code.
rule.ELEC-301.prompt.violation: Renderer code directly imports privileged Node.js built-ins such as fs, child_process, or net.
rule.ELEC-301.prompt.requirement: Electron renderer code must stay isolated from privileged Node APIs.
rule.ELEC-301.prompt.solution: Move the privileged capability into preload or main and expose the minimal method surface through a safe bridge.
rule.ELEC-302.intent: Renderer code should not import the electron package directly for IPC or shell access.
rule.ELEC-302.fix: Wrap renderer-side IPC usage behind preload-exposed service modules instead of importing electron directly.
rule.ELEC-302.prompt.violation: Renderer code directly imports the electron package.
rule.ELEC-302.prompt.requirement: Renderer code should consume a narrow preload bridge instead of direct electron APIs.
rule.ELEC-302.prompt.solution: Replace direct electron imports with bridge methods defined in preload and typed service helpers.
rule.ELEC-303.intent: Preload should expose a narrow, typed bridge rather than raw privileged Electron or Node capabilities.
rule.ELEC-303.fix: Expose only minimal typed methods through contextBridge and keep raw privileged objects private.
rule.ELEC-303.prompt.violation: Preload appears to expose raw privileged capabilities directly to window.
rule.ELEC-303.prompt.requirement: Preload must expose only a narrow, reviewed bridge surface to renderer code.
rule.ELEC-303.prompt.solution: Replace broad raw capability exposure with minimal typed bridge methods and strict input validation.
rule.VSCODE-301.intent: Command registrations should delegate heavy logic to services instead of embedding large workflows inline.
rule.VSCODE-301.fix: Move workspace mutation, network orchestration, and business branching out of command registration callbacks into service modules.
rule.VSCODE-301.prompt.violation: A VS Code command handler appears to contain heavy orchestration inline.
rule.VSCODE-301.prompt.requirement: Commands should stay thin and delegate work to reusable services.
rule.VSCODE-301.prompt.solution: Extract the heavy workflow into a service and keep the command callback responsible only for wiring and user interaction.
rule.VSCODE-302.intent: Webview content must avoid unsafe remote scripts and inline script patterns without a safe CSP/nonce model.
rule.VSCODE-302.fix: Serve local trusted assets, add CSP/nonce protection, and remove unsafe remote or inline script construction.
rule.VSCODE-302.prompt.violation: A VS Code webview appears to embed unsafe remote or inline script content.
rule.VSCODE-302.prompt.requirement: Webviews must use trusted local assets and a safe CSP/nonce model.
rule.VSCODE-302.prompt.solution: Move scripts to trusted packaged assets, add CSP/nonce handling, and remove unsafe inline or remote script usage.
rule.VSCODE-303.intent: Extension and webview message handlers must validate workspace paths, URIs, and shell-like inputs before use.
rule.VSCODE-303.fix: Centralize validation and policy checks for workspace paths, URIs, and command inputs before performing file or process actions.
rule.VSCODE-303.prompt.violation: A VS Code extension path appears to trust unvalidated workspace or shell-related input.
rule.VSCODE-303.prompt.requirement: Workspace, URI, and command inputs must be validated and policy-checked before use.
rule.VSCODE-303.prompt.solution: Add explicit validation and allow-list checks before file access, process execution, or webview message handling.
rule.NODE-ARCH-101.intent: Transport-facing Node.js modules must not import repositories or raw data clients directly.
rule.NODE-ARCH-101.fix: Move persistence access into service modules and let transport layers depend on services instead of repositories.
rule.NODE-ARCH-101.prompt.violation: A transport-facing Node.js module imports repositories or raw data clients directly.
rule.NODE-ARCH-101.prompt.requirement: Routes, controllers, and handlers must delegate persistence access through services.
rule.NODE-ARCH-101.prompt.solution: Move the data access logic into a service and inject or import that service from the transport layer.
rule.NODE-ARCH-102.intent: Transport handlers should stay thin and avoid mixing validation, orchestration, persistence, and response shaping in one function.
rule.NODE-ARCH-102.fix: Split request wiring from business orchestration and move reusable logic into service modules.
rule.NODE-ARCH-102.prompt.violation: A transport handler appears to mix too many responsibilities inline.
rule.NODE-ARCH-102.prompt.requirement: Transport code should stay thin and delegate business orchestration to services.
rule.NODE-ARCH-102.prompt.solution: Extract validation, orchestration, and persistence logic into services and keep the handler focused on transport concerns.
rule.NODE-ERR-201.intent: Async handlers should propagate errors into centralized error handling instead of swallowing them locally.
rule.NODE-ERR-201.fix: Forward errors to centralized middleware or framework error boundaries and avoid empty or log-only catch blocks.
rule.NODE-ERR-201.prompt.violation: An async Node.js handler appears to swallow or locally bury errors.
rule.NODE-ERR-201.prompt.requirement: Async handlers must propagate failures into centralized error handling.
rule.NODE-ERR-201.prompt.solution: Re-throw, return next(error), or delegate to framework error boundaries instead of swallowing the failure.
rule.NODE-SEC-202.intent: Sensitive credentials and tokens must not be logged from Node.js services.
rule.NODE-SEC-202.fix: Remove or redact sensitive values before logging and centralize safe logging helpers.
rule.NODE-SEC-202.prompt.violation: A logging statement appears to expose credentials or security-sensitive values.
rule.NODE-SEC-202.prompt.requirement: Logs must not leak passwords, tokens, cookies, or authorization data.
rule.NODE-SEC-202.prompt.solution: Redact or remove sensitive fields and use safe structured logging helpers instead.
rule.NODE-PERF-301.intent: Outbound network calls should use explicit timeouts, abort signals, or bounded retry behavior.
rule.NODE-PERF-301.fix: Introduce timeout, abort, and bounded retry controls for outbound HTTP/RPC clients.
rule.NODE-PERF-301.prompt.violation: An outbound Node.js network path appears to lack timeout or bounded retry controls.
rule.NODE-PERF-301.prompt.requirement: External calls must have explicit failure bounds so they cannot hang indefinitely.
rule.NODE-PERF-301.prompt.solution: Add timeout/abort controls and keep retries bounded and observable.
rule.EXPRESS-301.intent: Express route handlers should stay thin and delegate business workflows to services.
rule.EXPRESS-301.fix: Move orchestration and business branching out of route callbacks into services and middleware.
rule.EXPRESS-301.prompt.violation: An Express route handler appears to contain heavy workflow logic inline.
rule.EXPRESS-301.prompt.requirement: Route handlers should focus on request wiring and delegate business workflows.
rule.EXPRESS-301.prompt.solution: Extract the heavy route logic into services and keep middleware/handlers transport-focused.
rule.EXPRESS-302.intent: Express handlers should not send a response and continue control flow without an explicit return or error transfer.
rule.EXPRESS-302.fix: Make response termination explicit and avoid fallthrough after res.send/res.json/res.end or next(error).
rule.EXPRESS-302.prompt.violation: An Express handler appears to risk double-send or hidden fallthrough after responding.
rule.EXPRESS-302.prompt.requirement: Response termination must be explicit so handlers do not continue unexpectedly.
rule.EXPRESS-302.prompt.solution: Add explicit returns or restructure the control flow so no code path continues after the response is finalized.
rule.NEST-301.intent: NestJS controllers must not inject repositories or raw data-layer services directly.
rule.NEST-301.fix: Inject providers/services into controllers and keep repository access inside providers.
rule.NEST-301.prompt.violation: A NestJS controller appears to inject a repository or raw data-layer dependency directly.
rule.NEST-301.prompt.requirement: Controllers must depend on providers/services, not repositories or raw data clients.
rule.NEST-301.prompt.solution: Move data access into a provider and inject that provider into the controller instead.
rule.NEST-302.intent: NestJS controllers should stay thin and avoid inline business orchestration.
rule.NEST-302.fix: Keep controllers focused on transport concerns and move workflows into providers and interceptors.
rule.NEST-302.prompt.violation: A NestJS controller appears to perform business orchestration inline.
rule.NEST-302.prompt.requirement: Controllers should stay thin and delegate workflows to providers.
rule.NEST-302.prompt.solution: Move orchestration, branching, and persistence logic into providers or interceptors and keep the controller thin.
prompt.audit.system: You are a strict AI coding governance auditor. Before auditing code, consume the project rule system in this order: 1) .ai-rules/rules-config.json defines enabledRuleIds, severityThreshold, detectOptions, thresholds, exceptions, and prompt behavior. 2) .ai-rules/config.json defines local project layout overrides such as pathAliases. Resolve aliases such as @service, @controller, @api, or @components before reasoning about paths; do not assume the template default layout when config.json provides a different mapping. 3) .ai-rules/.ai-rules.md defines rule severity, scope, intent, detect, fix, prompt, and context. Only audit enabled rules, treat context as supporting assets rather than the only scan target, honor detect.where when present, and never report paths covered by exceptions.
prompt.audit.user: Audit the target code against the resolved AI-RULES configuration. For regex/import/include rules, prioritize concrete local evidence. For ast/semantic rules, use careful AI judgment and reflect confidence honestly. If a context path does not exist, do not ignore the rule; use config.json pathAliases and the nearby project structure to infer the intended layer. Return only the required JSON report schema, with one enabled ruleId per issue and no extra prose.
prompt.repair.system: You are a code repair assistant. Follow the resolved AI-RULES configuration, including rules-config.json, config.json pathAliases, enabledRuleIds, severityThreshold, exceptions, rule intent, fix guidance, prompt requirements, and context assets. Produce executable minimal-change fixes and do not refactor unrelated code.
prompt.repair.user: Based on the violated rule metadata, report evidence, and resolved project context assets, generate a minimal patch plan and include patch-ready edits when helpful. Preserve architecture boundaries, respect exceptions, and avoid broad rewrites unrelated to the selected issue.
prompt.audit.cli: Start a semantic audit: read .ai-rules rules and configuration in the project, check code against architectural intent, and output ai-rule-report.json. Return strict JSON with this shape: { "version": "1.0", "violations": [ { "issueId": "ISSUE-001", "ruleId": "ARCH-101", "severity": "FATAL|WARN|INFO", "file": "src/...", "line": 1, "description": "...", "fixSuggestion": "...", "repairPrompt": "..." } ] }. Each violation must include a unique issueId and a repairPrompt.
prompt.logic.system: You are a business-logic vulnerability auditor. Use the compiled AI-RULES rule context, validator artifacts, and local evidence as supporting signals, but prioritize cross-file reasoning about authorization, ownership, state transitions, idempotency, tenant isolation, and trust boundaries.
prompt.logic.user: Inspect the target project for logic vulnerabilities rather than only framework misuse. Focus on workflow bypasses, missing ownership checks, unsafe status transitions, replay/idempotency holes, and inconsistencies between validation, permissions, and persistence. Return only the required JSON schema.
prompt.logic.c-cpp.system: You are a native-code logic and security auditor. Use the compiled AI-RULES rule context, validator artifacts, and local evidence as supporting signals, but prioritize cross-file reasoning about resource ownership, lifetime transitions, error propagation, lock discipline, parser boundaries, privileged operations, and partial cleanup paths.
prompt.logic.c-cpp.user: Inspect the C/C++ project for native logic and security flaws rather than generic style issues. Focus on ownership-transfer mistakes, unchecked critical return values, inconsistent lock or atomic protocols, parser length/offset/state validation gaps, trust-boundary failures around file/process/socket operations, and cleanup or rollback inconsistencies. Return only the required JSON schema.
prompt.logic.cli: Start a business-logic inspection: read the project .ai-rules configuration, compiled rule artifacts, and validator output, then produce ai-logic-report.json. Return strict JSON only with this shape: { "version": "1.0", "risks": [ { "issueId": "LOGIC-001", "category": "authz|ownership|state-machine|idempotency|consistency|input-trust|tenant-isolation|workflow|resource-lifetime|error-propagation|concurrency-protocol|parser-boundary|privilege-boundary|cleanup-consistency", "ruleId": "optional", "severity": "FATAL|WARN|INFO", "confidence": 0.0, "files": ["src/..."], "description": "...", "businessImpact": "...", "exploitPath": "...", "fixSuggestion": "...", "repairPrompt": "..." } ] }. Each risk must include a unique issueId.
template.c-cpp.title: AI-RULES C/C++ Template
template.c-cpp.desc.1: This template governs architecture, safety, concurrency, and build quality for C/C++ projects.
template.c-cpp.desc.2: Rules use the RULE block syntax with content keys separated from structure.
template.c-cpp.desc.3: Patterns in detect are illustrative and can be enhanced by AST/semantic analysis in CLI.
rule.CPP-ARCH-101.intent: Application and domain layers must not call platform-specific APIs directly.
rule.CPP-ARCH-101.fix: Wrap platform capabilities behind adapter interfaces and depend on abstractions.
rule.CPP-ARCH-101.prompt.violation: Detected direct dependency on platform implementation from upper layers.
rule.CPP-ARCH-101.prompt.requirement: Platform capabilities must be isolated via adapters.
rule.CPP-ARCH-101.prompt.solution: Introduce adapter abstractions and replace direct platform calls.
rule.CPP-ARCH-102.intent: Disallow reverse layering dependencies (e.g., domain depending on infra details).
rule.CPP-ARCH-102.fix: Apply dependency inversion and converge upper layers to interfaces.
rule.CPP-ARCH-102.prompt.solution: Move concrete details down to infra and depend on contracts.
rule.CPP-MEM-201.intent: Disallow raw new/delete; prefer RAII and smart pointers.
rule.CPP-MEM-201.fix: Replace raw ownership with unique_ptr/shared_ptr or stack allocation.
rule.CPP-MEM-201.prompt.requirement: Resource lifetime must be managed via RAII.
rule.CPP-MEM-201.prompt.solution: Refactor ownership using smart pointers and explicit lifetime semantics.
rule.CPP-MEM-202.intent: Do not return dangling pointers or references.
rule.CPP-MEM-202.fix: Use value semantics, smart pointers, or extend object lifetime safely.
rule.CPP-MEM-202.prompt.requirement: Returned objects must have safe lifetime guarantees.
rule.CPP-MEM-202.prompt.solution: Adjust return strategy and repair lifetime boundaries.
rule.CPP-MEM-203.intent: File/socket/lock handles must be wrapped by RAII types.
rule.CPP-MEM-203.fix: Introduce resource wrappers with deterministic release in destructors.
rule.CPP-MEM-203.prompt.violation: Detected unmanaged resource handles without RAII.
rule.CPP-MEM-203.prompt.requirement: Resource release must be automatic and predictable.
rule.CPP-MEM-203.prompt.solution: Create guard/wrapper types and remove manual release patterns.
rule.CPP-CONC-301.intent: Shared mutable state access must use synchronization strategy.
rule.CPP-CONC-301.fix: Protect shared state with mutex/atomic or lock-free safe structures.
rule.CPP-CONC-301.prompt.violation: Detected unsynchronized access to shared mutable state.
rule.CPP-CONC-301.prompt.requirement: Concurrent read/write operations must be thread-safe.
rule.CPP-CONC-301.prompt.solution: Add synchronization primitives and validate memory visibility.
rule.CPP-CONC-302.intent: Do not run blocking I/O while holding locks.
rule.CPP-CONC-302.fix: Reduce lock scope or move blocking I/O outside critical sections.
rule.CPP-CONC-302.prompt.violation: Detected blocking I/O inside lock scope.
rule.CPP-CONC-302.prompt.requirement: Critical sections should stay minimal and non-blocking.
rule.CPP-CONC-302.prompt.solution: Refactor critical section boundaries and reduce lock contention.
rule.CPP-CONC-303.intent: Shared-state updates must follow one consistent lock or atomic protocol across related code paths.
rule.CPP-CONC-303.fix: Unify the synchronization strategy so the same state is always protected by the same mutex, guard, or atomic contract.
rule.CPP-CONC-303.prompt.violation: Detected inconsistent synchronization discipline around shared state.
rule.CPP-CONC-303.prompt.requirement: Shared mutable state must use one explicit concurrency protocol across all entry points.
rule.CPP-CONC-303.prompt.solution: Converge lock ownership and atomic rules, then verify all read/write paths follow the same protocol.
rule.CPP-API-401.intent: Function error paths must be explicit.
rule.CPP-API-401.fix: Standardize failures using error codes, exceptions, or expected-like types.
rule.CPP-API-401.prompt.violation: Detected implicit or unclear error path handling.
rule.CPP-API-401.prompt.requirement: Callers must be able to detect and handle failures.
rule.CPP-API-401.prompt.solution: Define a consistent error contract and update call sites.
rule.CPP-API-402.intent: Public APIs should enforce const correctness and noexcept policy.
rule.CPP-API-402.fix: Add const to non-mutating methods and define explicit noexcept semantics.
rule.CPP-API-402.prompt.requirement: API contracts should be stable and exception behavior predictable.
rule.CPP-API-402.prompt.solution: Complete const/noexcept declarations and align implementation.
rule.CPP-BUILD-501.intent: Build must enable strict warnings and treat them as errors.
rule.CPP-BUILD-501.prompt.requirement: Compiler diagnostics must be enforced strictly.
rule.CPP-BUILD-501.prompt.solution: Add strict flags and clean existing warnings.
rule.CPP-BUILD-502.intent: All targets must use a unified C++ standard version.
rule.CPP-BUILD-502.fix: Set and enforce one C++ standard for all targets.
rule.CPP-BUILD-502.prompt.violation: Detected inconsistent C++ standard settings across targets.
rule.CPP-BUILD-502.prompt.requirement: Targets should share consistent standard settings to avoid ABI/behavior drift.
rule.CPP-BUILD-502.prompt.solution: Normalize standard configuration and validate full build.
rule.CPP-SEC-601.fix: Replace with bounded and safer alternatives.
rule.CPP-SEC-601.prompt.requirement: Memory and input operations must enforce bounds safety.
rule.CPP-SEC-601.prompt.solution: Use safe API replacements and add explicit length checks.
rule.CPP-SEC-602.intent: External input must be validated for length and format.
rule.CPP-SEC-602.fix: Apply boundary and format validation before processing input.
rule.CPP-SEC-602.prompt.requirement: Input data must be validated before use.
rule.CPP-SEC-602.prompt.solution: Add validation paths and reject invalid data early.
rule.CPP-LOGIC-801.intent: Resource ownership and release paths must stay explicit across create, transfer, cleanup, and rollback flows.
rule.CPP-LOGIC-801.fix: Make ownership transfer explicit and centralize cleanup paths with RAII guards or one deterministic release policy.
rule.CPP-LOGIC-801.prompt.violation: Detected a likely ownership or cleanup-path inconsistency.
rule.CPP-LOGIC-801.prompt.requirement: Resource lifetime transitions must be explicit and safe across success, failure, and rollback paths.
rule.CPP-LOGIC-801.prompt.solution: Refactor ownership transfer, cleanup ordering, and failure handling so every path has one clear lifetime contract.
rule.CPP-ERR-303.intent: Critical return values and error statuses must be checked and propagated on privileged or state-changing paths.
rule.CPP-ERR-303.fix: Check the return value immediately, map failures into one error contract, and stop unsafe follow-up actions on failure.
rule.CPP-ERR-303.prompt.violation: Detected a likely ignored critical return value or error status.
rule.CPP-ERR-303.prompt.requirement: Failure signals on security-sensitive or state-changing paths must be handled explicitly before execution continues.
rule.CPP-ERR-303.prompt.solution: Introduce explicit failure checks, propagate diagnostics, and block subsequent side effects when the critical call fails.
rule.CPP-SEC-603.intent: Privileged file, process, and socket operations must validate trust boundaries before executing.
rule.CPP-SEC-603.fix: Validate paths, targets, modes, identities, and execution assumptions before opening files, spawning processes, or mutating privileged resources.
rule.CPP-SEC-603.prompt.violation: Detected a privileged operation that appears to trust unchecked external state.
rule.CPP-SEC-603.prompt.requirement: Privileged operations must verify input trust, target safety, and execution preconditions before they mutate the system.
rule.CPP-SEC-603.prompt.solution: Add trust-boundary validation and reject unsafe paths, targets, or execution states before the operation runs.
rule.CPP-SEC-604.intent: Parsers, decoders, and binary readers must validate offsets, lengths, and state transitions before advancing.
rule.CPP-SEC-604.fix: Guard every offset/length/state transition with explicit bounds validation and fail closed on malformed input.
rule.CPP-SEC-604.prompt.violation: Detected a parser or decoder path that may advance without validating bounds or state transitions.
rule.CPP-SEC-604.prompt.requirement: Parsing logic must validate offsets, lengths, and state-machine assumptions before consuming untrusted data.
rule.CPP-SEC-604.prompt.solution: Introduce explicit boundary/state guards and reject malformed input before any unsafe read, copy, or transition occurs.
rule.CPP-TEST-701.intent: Core module changes must include unit/regression tests.
rule.CPP-TEST-701.fix: Add minimal verifiable tests for changed critical paths.
rule.CPP-TEST-701.prompt.violation: Detected core changes without corresponding tests.
rule.CPP-TEST-701.prompt.solution: Add targeted tests and verify before merge.

rule.JAVA-ARCH-101.intent: Controllers must not depend on repositories directly.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-101.fix: Move business/data access logic into service layer.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-101.prompt.violation: Detected direct data-layer access from controller.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-101.prompt.requirement: Layering must follow Controller -> Service -> Repository.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-101.prompt.solution: Refactor data access into service and call service from controller.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-102.intent: Do not instantiate repositories or data objects in controller layer.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-102.fix: Use dependency injection and depend on service contracts.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-102.prompt.violation: Detected cross-layer object construction in controller.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-102.prompt.requirement: Controller layer should only orchestrate request/response flow.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-102.prompt.solution: Remove cross-layer dependencies and inject service abstractions.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-103.intent: Controllers should not contain business branching or orchestration logic that belongs in services.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-103.fix: Move business decision logic and orchestration into the service layer.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-103.prompt.violation: Detected business logic or branching inside a controller method.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-103.prompt.requirement: Controllers should stay thin and delegate business logic to services.
rule.JAVA-ARCH-103.prompt.solution: Extract branching and orchestration into a service method.
rule.JAVA-SEC-201.intent: Disallow SQL construction via string concatenation.
rule.JAVA-SEC-201.fix: Use parameterized queries or safe ORM query APIs.
rule.JAVA-SEC-201.prompt.solution: Refactor query logic to use bound parameters.
rule.JAVA-SEC-203.intent: Global exception handlers must not expose stack traces or internal error details to API callers.
rule.JAVA-SEC-203.fix: Return sanitized error payloads and move stack traces to internal logs only.
rule.JAVA-SEC-203.prompt.violation: Detected exception handling that may leak internal stack or implementation details.
rule.JAVA-SEC-203.prompt.requirement: External error responses must not reveal internal stack traces or sensitive diagnostics.
rule.JAVA-SEC-203.prompt.solution: Sanitize API error responses and keep detailed diagnostics in logs.
rule.JAVA-SEC-204.intent: Logs must not include passwords, tokens, authorization headers, or other sensitive credential fields.
rule.JAVA-SEC-204.fix: Mask or remove sensitive fields before logging and standardize secure logging helpers.
rule.JAVA-SEC-204.prompt.violation: Detected logging pattern that may expose sensitive credentials or secrets.
rule.JAVA-SEC-204.prompt.requirement: Production logs must avoid leaking sensitive authentication or credential material.
rule.JAVA-SEC-204.prompt.solution: Redact sensitive fields and log only safe identifiers or metadata.
rule.JAVA-SEC-205.intent: Sensitive Spring endpoints must enforce authentication and authorization instead of relying on open-by-default access.
rule.JAVA-SEC-205.fix: Protect sensitive endpoints with explicit authentication/authorization policies such as method security, request matchers, or shared access guards.
rule.JAVA-SEC-205.prompt.violation: Detected a controller path that appears externally reachable but lacks clear authentication or authorization enforcement.
rule.JAVA-SEC-205.prompt.requirement: Sensitive API endpoints must have explicit access control and must not rely on permissive defaults.
rule.JAVA-SEC-205.prompt.solution: Add explicit authorization rules and align endpoint exposure with least-privilege policies.
rule.JAVA-SEC-206.intent: Spring security configuration must not broadly permit all traffic or disable core protections without narrow justification.
rule.JAVA-SEC-206.fix: Constrain permitAll usage, limit ignored matchers, and keep CSRF/authentication protections enabled unless there is a narrowly documented exception.
rule.JAVA-SEC-206.prompt.violation: Detected a Spring security configuration that may be overly permissive.
rule.JAVA-SEC-206.prompt.requirement: Security configuration must preserve least-privilege access and should not disable protections globally.
rule.JAVA-SEC-206.prompt.solution: Tighten security matchers, reduce open endpoints, and document any narrowly scoped exceptions.
rule.JAVA-SEC-202.intent: Disallow overly permissive CORS settings (e.g., origins=*).
rule.JAVA-SEC-202.fix: Restrict trusted origins and isolate config per environment.
rule.JAVA-SEC-202.prompt.requirement: CORS policy must follow least privilege.
rule.JAVA-SEC-202.prompt.solution: Use explicit origin allowlist and environment-specific config.
rule.JAVA-API-301.intent: RequestBody inputs should be validated with @Valid.
rule.JAVA-API-301.fix: Add validation annotations on DTOs and enforce @Valid at entry.
rule.JAVA-API-301.prompt.requirement: External input must be validated before business execution.
rule.JAVA-API-301.prompt.solution: Add DTO constraints and @Valid in controller signatures.
rule.JAVA-API-302.intent: API responses should use DTOs instead of exposing entities directly.
rule.JAVA-API-302.fix: Introduce DTO mapping and hide internal entity fields.
rule.JAVA-API-302.prompt.requirement: API contracts must stay decoupled from persistence models.
rule.JAVA-API-302.prompt.solution: Return DTOs and control serialized fields explicitly.
rule.JAVA-DATA-401.intent: Write operations must define explicit transaction boundaries.
rule.JAVA-DATA-401.fix: Add transaction semantics on write service methods.
rule.JAVA-DATA-401.prompt.violation: Detected write path without transaction semantics.
rule.JAVA-DATA-401.prompt.requirement: Consistency-sensitive operations must run in transactions.
rule.JAVA-DATA-401.prompt.solution: Add transaction annotations and verify rollback behavior.
rule.JAVA-DATA-403.intent: Transactional boundaries must not be declared on controllers.
rule.JAVA-DATA-403.fix: Move transaction management to the service layer and keep controllers free of transaction semantics.
rule.JAVA-DATA-403.prompt.requirement: Transaction boundaries belong in application/service layers, not controllers.
rule.JAVA-DATA-403.prompt.solution: Remove controller-level transaction handling and move it to services.
rule.JAVA-DATA-404.intent: Write service methods must define explicit transaction boundaries.
rule.JAVA-DATA-404.fix: Add explicit transactional semantics on write-oriented service methods.
rule.JAVA-DATA-404.prompt.violation: Detected write service logic without an explicit transaction boundary.
rule.JAVA-DATA-404.prompt.requirement: Write operations must run with clear transaction semantics.
rule.JAVA-DATA-404.prompt.solution: Add or refine transaction annotations on the service write path.
rule.JAVA-PERF-701.intent: Loops must not perform unbounded remote HTTP, RPC, or client calls without batching, timeouts, and concurrency control.
rule.JAVA-PERF-701.fix: Batch remote work, move repeated calls behind a service/client abstraction, and add timeout, retry, and rate-limit safeguards.
rule.JAVA-PERF-701.prompt.violation: Detected a loop that appears to perform remote calls without clear bounding controls.
rule.JAVA-PERF-701.prompt.requirement: Remote calls inside loops must be bounded, observable, timeout-protected, and preferably batched.
rule.JAVA-PERF-701.prompt.solution: Refactor the loop to use batching or controlled concurrency and enforce client-level timeout/retry policies.
rule.JAVA-ERR-602.intent: Business exceptions and system/infrastructure failures must remain distinguishable in service and API error handling.
rule.JAVA-ERR-602.fix: Introduce explicit business exception types or error codes, translate infrastructure errors separately, and sanitize external API responses.
rule.JAVA-ERR-602.prompt.violation: Detected error handling that may collapse business and system failures into a generic exception or response.
rule.JAVA-ERR-602.prompt.requirement: Business-rule failures, validation failures, and infrastructure failures must be represented and handled separately.
rule.JAVA-ERR-602.prompt.solution: Separate exception classes or error codes and update the global handler to return stable sanitized API errors.
rule.JAVA-DATA-402.intent: Disallow unbounded full-table reads in service layer.
rule.JAVA-DATA-402.fix: Use pagination and enforce default page limits.
rule.JAVA-DATA-402.prompt.requirement: List queries must be paginated and bounded.
rule.JAVA-DATA-402.prompt.solution: Introduce paging params and safe defaults.
rule.JAVA-TEST-501.intent: Core business changes must include tests.
rule.JAVA-TEST-501.fix: Add service/controller unit or integration tests.
rule.JAVA-TEST-501.prompt.violation: Detected core changes without test coverage.
rule.JAVA-TEST-501.prompt.solution: Add focused tests and validate pass status.
rule.JAVA-OBS-601.intent: Critical business paths should emit structured logs.
rule.JAVA-OBS-601.fix: Add structured logs with contextual fields and error metadata.
rule.JAVA-OBS-601.prompt.violation: Detected insufficient logs in critical path.
rule.JAVA-OBS-601.prompt.solution: Add standardized structured logging on key branches.

rule.PYBASE-CODE-101.fix: Catch explicit exception types and log useful context.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-101.prompt.solution: Replace with explicit exception classes and add logging.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-102.fix: Use None as default and initialize inside function body.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-102.prompt.requirement: Default arguments must avoid shared mutable state.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-102.prompt.solution: Switch to None + local initialization pattern.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-103.intent: Functions should stay below the configured line-count threshold.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-103.fix: Split oversized functions into focused helpers or extract cohesive subroutines.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-103.prompt.violation: Detected a function that exceeds the configured line-count threshold.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-103.prompt.requirement: Functions should remain small enough to review, test, and reason about safely.
rule.PYBASE-CODE-103.prompt.solution: Break the function into smaller units with clearer responsibilities.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-201.intent: Public functions should define parameter and return type hints.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-201.fix: Add type hints to public APIs.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-201.prompt.violation: Detected public function without type hints.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-201.prompt.requirement: Public contracts should be explicit and typed.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-202.fix: Prefer concrete types, protocols, or bounded generics.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-202.prompt.requirement: Type system should represent real constraints.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-202.prompt.solution: Replace Any with precise type definitions.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-203.intent: Function signatures should stay below the configured parameter-count threshold.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-203.fix: Group related parameters into value objects, config objects, or smaller abstractions.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-203.prompt.violation: Detected a function signature with too many parameters.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-203.prompt.requirement: Function APIs should remain easy to understand and hard to misuse.
rule.PYBASE-TYPE-203.prompt.solution: Reduce parameter count by introducing focused data structures or narrower APIs.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-301.fix: Use safe parsing alternatives (e.g., ast.literal_eval or whitelist interpreters).
rule.PYBASE-SEC-301.prompt.requirement: Untrusted input must never reach dynamic execution.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-301.prompt.solution: Replace dynamic execution and validate input rigorously.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-302.fix: Use safer serialization formats or signed payload validation.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-302.prompt.requirement: Deserialization must verify source and integrity.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-302.prompt.solution: Switch serialization strategy and add integrity checks.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-303.intent: Do not use weak hashing algorithms such as MD5 or SHA1 for password or credential handling.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-303.fix: Use a password-safe hashing library such as bcrypt, scrypt, argon2, or a framework-approved password encoder.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-303.prompt.violation: Detected weak hashing algorithm usage in security-sensitive code.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-303.prompt.requirement: Password and credential material must use modern, password-safe hashing.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-303.prompt.solution: Replace weak hashing with a modern password hashing strategy.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-304.intent: Logs must not include secrets, tokens, passwords, or credential-like fields.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-304.fix: Mask or remove sensitive fields before logging and centralize secure log serialization if possible.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-304.prompt.violation: Detected logging pattern that may expose sensitive data.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-304.prompt.requirement: Application logs must avoid leaking secrets or credential material.
rule.PYBASE-SEC-304.prompt.solution: Redact sensitive values and log only safe metadata.
rule.PYBASE-TEST-401.intent: Core module changes should include tests.
rule.PYBASE-TEST-401.fix: Add unit/regression tests for critical branches.
rule.PYBASE-TEST-401.prompt.violation: Detected core change without test coverage.
rule.PYBASE-TEST-401.prompt.solution: Add focused tests and verify passing results.
rule.PYBASE-REPRO-501.intent: Training/experiment entrypoints should control random seeds for reproducibility.
rule.PYBASE-REPRO-501.fix: Set and centralize random/numpy/torch seeds at entrypoint.
rule.PYBASE-REPRO-501.prompt.violation: Detected missing reproducibility control in experiment entrypoint.
rule.PYBASE-REPRO-501.prompt.requirement: Results should be reproducible and comparable.
rule.PYBASE-REPRO-501.prompt.solution: Add unified seed settings and record them in logs.
rule.PYBASE-ERR-601.intent: Broad exceptions must not be swallowed silently.
rule.PYBASE-ERR-601.fix: Log, translate, or re-raise broad exceptions instead of suppressing them.
rule.PYBASE-ERR-601.prompt.violation: Detected broad exception handling that appears to swallow failures.
rule.PYBASE-ERR-601.prompt.requirement: Exceptions must preserve diagnosability and failure semantics.
rule.PYBASE-ERR-601.prompt.solution: Add logging, raise a domain error, or re-raise instead of suppressing the exception.
rule.PYBASE-IO-602.intent: External HTTP calls must define explicit timeouts.
rule.PYBASE-IO-602.fix: Add request timeouts and centralize HTTP client configuration where possible.
rule.PYBASE-IO-602.prompt.violation: Detected external HTTP usage without an explicit timeout policy.
rule.PYBASE-IO-602.prompt.requirement: External I/O must fail fast and predictably.
rule.PYBASE-IO-602.prompt.solution: Set explicit timeout values and move shared configuration into a central client layer.
rule.PY-ARCH-101.intent: Route handlers must not create DB sessions or access data layer directly.
rule.PY-ARCH-101.fix: Move data access into service/repository layers.
rule.PY-ARCH-101.prompt.violation: Detected direct database access from API layer.
rule.PY-ARCH-101.prompt.requirement: Layering must follow Router -> Service -> Repository.
rule.PY-ARCH-101.prompt.solution: Refactor DB operations out of route handlers.
rule.PY-ARCH-102.intent: Route handlers should not depend on repositories directly.
rule.PY-ARCH-102.fix: Expose business capabilities through service layer.
rule.PY-ARCH-102.prompt.requirement: API layer should orchestrate IO boundaries only.
rule.PY-ARCH-102.prompt.solution: Adjust dependency direction via service abstractions.
rule.PY-SEC-202.intent: Disallow disabled JWT verification or permissive CORS defaults.
rule.PY-SEC-202.fix: Enable verification and restrict CORS to trusted origins.
rule.PY-SEC-202.prompt.requirement: Security config must follow least privilege.
rule.PY-SEC-202.prompt.solution: Harden auth and CORS configuration per environment.
rule.PY-SEC-203.intent: Do not construct SQL statements with string interpolation, concatenation, or f-strings in FastAPI application code.
rule.PY-SEC-203.fix: Use parameterized queries, SQLAlchemy bind parameters, or ORM query builders instead of string-built SQL.
rule.PY-SEC-203.prompt.violation: Detected likely SQL construction through string interpolation or concatenation.
rule.PY-SEC-203.prompt.requirement: Database queries must be parameterized and must not embed user-controlled values directly into SQL strings.
rule.PY-SEC-203.prompt.solution: Refactor the query path to use bound parameters or safe ORM query composition.
rule.PY-SEC-204.intent: FastAPI request handling and logging must not record raw passwords, tokens, cookies, authorization headers, or credential payloads.
rule.PY-SEC-204.fix: Redact sensitive fields before logging, and centralize safe request logging or tracing helpers.
rule.PY-SEC-204.prompt.violation: Detected request logging or tracing that may expose sensitive authentication material.
rule.PY-SEC-204.prompt.requirement: API logs and traces must avoid leaking secrets, tokens, cookies, or credential-bearing payloads.
rule.PY-SEC-204.prompt.solution: Mask sensitive fields and keep only safe metadata such as request IDs, actor IDs, and bounded diagnostics.
rule.PY-API-301.intent: Endpoint inputs should be defined and validated by Pydantic models.
rule.PY-API-301.fix: Add schema models for body/query inputs and enforce validation.
rule.PY-API-301.prompt.requirement: Inputs must be structured and validated.
rule.PY-API-301.prompt.solution: Bind Pydantic schemas to endpoint signatures.
rule.PY-API-302.intent: Endpoints should use response_model instead of returning ORM objects directly.
rule.PY-API-302.fix: Define response schemas and map ORM to API models.
rule.PY-API-302.prompt.requirement: Response contracts must be stable and explicit.
rule.PY-API-302.prompt.solution: Add response_model and control field exposure.
rule.PY-API-303.intent: FastAPI endpoints should declare explicit response_model contracts.
rule.PY-API-303.fix: Add response_model declarations so the API surface is explicit and validated.
rule.PY-API-303.prompt.violation: Detected endpoint without an explicit response_model contract.
rule.PY-API-303.prompt.requirement: API responses should be explicit, validated, and documented.
rule.PY-API-303.prompt.solution: Declare a response_model and return data that conforms to it.
rule.PY-API-304.intent: List endpoints must enforce pagination or explicit limit bounds.
rule.PY-API-304.fix: Add pagination parameters or a bounded limit to list-style endpoints.
rule.PY-API-304.prompt.violation: Detected list endpoint that may return unbounded results.
rule.PY-API-304.prompt.requirement: Collection endpoints must be bounded and production-safe.
rule.PY-API-304.prompt.solution: Introduce pagination or enforce explicit limit guards on the endpoint.
rule.PY-ASYNC-401.intent: Do not use blocking HTTP clients inside async routes.
rule.PY-ASYNC-401.fix: Use async clients such as httpx.AsyncClient.
rule.PY-ASYNC-401.prompt.violation: Detected blocking I/O in async execution path.
rule.PY-ASYNC-401.prompt.requirement: Async path must avoid blocking operations.
rule.PY-ASYNC-401.prompt.solution: Replace blocking calls with async equivalents.
rule.PY-ASYNC-402.intent: Disallow time.sleep in async-capable code paths.
rule.PY-ASYNC-402.fix: Replace with asyncio.sleep or background task scheduling.
rule.PY-ASYNC-402.prompt.requirement: Event loop must remain schedulable and responsive.
rule.PY-ASYNC-402.prompt.solution: Refactor blocking waits to async-safe timing.
rule.PY-OBS-601.intent: Critical exception paths should emit structured logs.
rule.PY-OBS-601.fix: Add trace/context/error-code fields in standardized logs.
rule.PY-OBS-601.prompt.violation: Detected insufficient logging in critical flow.
rule.PY-OBS-601.prompt.solution: Add standardized structured logs on key branches.
prompt.setup.copilot: Create two reusable chat shortcuts for this repo in GitHub Copilot Chat: '/law-audit' and '/law-fix'. '/law-audit' should run: ai-law audit --locale en and then strictly return ai-rule-report.json in the required schema. '/law-fix' should ask for issueId first, then run: ai-law fix --issueId <ISSUE_ID>, and use the copied prompt to produce minimal patch-ready edits.
prompt.setup.codex: Create two reusable command prompts for Codex in this repo context: '/law-audit' and '/law-fix'. '/law-audit' executes ai-law audit --locale en and outputs ai-rule-report.json only. '/law-fix' asks for issueId, executes ai-law fix --issueId <ISSUE_ID>, and returns minimal architecture-safe code changes based on the copied prompt.
prompt.setup.cursor: Set up two reusable prompts in Cursor for this repo: 'law-audit' and 'law-fix'. 'law-audit' should run ai-law audit --locale en and output ai-rule-report.json strictly in JSON schema. 'law-fix' should ask for issueId, run ai-law fix --issueId <ISSUE_ID>, and then generate minimal patch-ready edits.
prompt.setup.claude-code: Set up three reusable Claude Code slash commands in this repo: '/law-audit', '/law-fix', and '/law-logic'. '/law-audit' should run ai-law audit --locale en, read the generated cache artifacts, and save the final strict JSON report as ai-rule-report.json. '/law-fix' should require an issueId, run ai-law validate-report, then run ai-law fix --issueId <ISSUE_ID> and apply only minimal architecture-preserving edits for that issue. '/law-logic' should run ai-law inspect-logic --locale en, read the logic cache artifacts, and save the final strict JSON report as ai-logic-report.json.
prompt.setup.custom: Configure your AI coding tool with two reusable actions in this repository: 'law-audit' and 'law-fix'. 'law-audit': run ai-law audit --locale en and output only ai-rule-report.json in the required schema. 'law-fix': ask for issueId, run ai-law fix --issueId <ISSUE_ID>, then generate the smallest safe patch from the copied prompt.
prompt.setup.noSlashHint: If this tool does not support real slash commands, save these as reusable prompt templates, snippets, or quick actions.
